requirements.evidence: Migration matches the schema, with unique(entity_id,email) and a cascade FK (migration:14-25). The model normalizes e-mail on saving (EntityInvite.php:28-34). sendInvite validates input, rejects existing members and pending invites, replaces expired invites, turns a QueryException into an error on inviteEmail, and records a rate-limit hit only after success (Members.php:43-111). accept/decline check the invitee, accept is idempotent and uses firstOrCreate (PendingInvites.php:14-73). Both mount and the route are manager-only (Members.php:39, routes/web.php:56). The modals use the required title keys, and the select has no empty option. Gaps: the members_title/invite_title/invite_submit ui keys are added but the view uses JSON keys instead. The title is rendered both in the header slot and in the card. The tenant session key 'current_entity_id' cannot be checked against the existing code.

conventions.evidence: No tests at all, which breaks the mandatory TDD rule. Domain writes are inline in Livewire components instead of app/Actions (EntityInvite::create in Members.php:89, EntityMembership::firstOrCreate in PendingInvites.php:33). Invite authorization is a hand-rolled abort_if(email !== ...) instead of a policy (PendingInvites.php:20,63). memberRole uses inline validateOnly rules rather than #[Validate] (Members.php:158-160). docs/business-rules.md is not updated for the invite rules. On the positive side: $fillable is set, CHANGELOG and database-schema.md are updated, Bulma modals are used and the generated-style migration has a down().

security.evidence: Every Members action except cancelRemoval authorizes 'update' on the entity. Parameters are resolved through $this->entity->memberships()/invites(), so foreign IDs fail. accept/decline check the invitee's e-mail server-side. Output is escaped with {{ }}. The invite rate limit is in place and owner is excluded from the allowed roles. Minor: selectedMembershipId and memberRole are client-writable and not #[Locked], but saveRole re-resolves and authorizes, so impact is limited. PendingInvites does not guard against a guest (auth()->user()->email on null).

tests.evidence: The diff has no test files. Nothing covers sendInvite, cancelInvite, accept/decline, the modal flow, the mail, the factory or the 403 on the route, and there are no unauthorized-call or tamper tests.

simplicity.evidence: The code is mostly direct. Small redundancies: e-mail is trimmed twice (Members.php:47 and 51) as well as in the model hook. The `role instanceof UserRole ? ->value : (string)` checks are defensive despite the enum cast (Members.php:141-143, PendingInvites.php:38-40, entity-invite.blade.php:4). isPending()/isExpired() are unused while the same query is written out three times.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and the style matches the existing component. sendInvite is long (about 70 lines). The ui keys members_title, members_invite_title, members_invite_submit and the en role keys are partly dead code. A helpful existing comment was removed from removeMember (the 'Never leave the entity without a manager' line).

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. lang/pt_BR.json re-escapes unrelated keys ('Press \/ to search', 'State \/ County', 'Zip \/ Postal Code', 'Uploading files... (:current\/:total)'), which adds unrelated churn. Existing explanatory comments are deleted.

issues.explanation: The change adds a whole invite feature without a single Pest test, including the unauthorized-call and tamper tests that the Livewire policy requires.
Invite creation and acceptance (membership creation) are domain writes done inline in components instead of app/Actions classes that authorize internally.
Invitee authorization is a hand-rolled abort_if e-mail comparison instead of a policy, against the 'authorization always goes through policies' rule.
memberRole is validated with inline validateOnly rules instead of #[Validate] on the property, and selectedMembershipId is a client-writable server context value without #[Locked].
accept/decline dereference auth()->user()->email without a guard, so an unauthenticated call fails with an error instead of a clean 403.
The ui.members_title, members_invite_title and members_invite_submit keys are added but unused (the view uses JSON keys), and the 'Members of :entity' title is rendered twice.
The new domain invariants (invite-only membership, 7-day expiry, manager-only members page) are not documented in business-rules.md.
Unrelated keys are re-encoded with escaped slashes, which adds noise to the diff.
isPending()/isExpired() are never used while the pending query is duplicated in Members::sendInvite, Members::render and PendingInvites::render.
An existing explanatory comment about keeping a manager was removed for no reason.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member adds with an invite flow: migration, model, factory, mailable, PendingInvites component and a manager-only members page with detail and removal modals. It covers most functional requirements, including the edge cases for races, rate limiting and idempotent accept. It ships no tests at all, puts domain writes inline instead of in Actions, and authorizes invitees without a policy, so it needs substantial rework before merging.
